candidates.name: usdot-jpo-codehub/rec-gov-analysis
candidates.what_it_holds: US DOT Volpe Center tooling (not a live scraper of Airbnb) for analyzing recreation.gov's own historical reservation exports from the RIDB portal (ridb.recreation.gov data-download page) across national forests/federal campgrounds, built for transportation-planning demand analysis. No data committed; points to a real point-in-time reservation-history download.
candidates.why_useful: Outdoor-recreation/camping booking curves are a public, government-hosted 'book-ahead' kernel analogue (like NCLH advance sales, item 18) with real reservation lead times and cancellation behavior; a cross-check on how far ahead US leisure travelers commit, useful context for the RNPL/booking-lead-time thesis and travel-volume seasonality even though it never touches Airbnb.
candidates.time_coverage: historical RIDB reservation exports, span not specified on page
candidates.size_hint: tooling repo only; data lives on ridb.recreation.gov

candidates.name: juftin/camply
candidates.what_it_holds: Actively maintained (651 stars) MIT-licensed campsite-availability finder hitting Recreation.gov's RIDB API plus state park systems (CA, FL, OH, VA, AZ), Yellowstone, Canadian and Australian parks; polls live availability/cancellation feeds.
candidates.why_useful: A maintained, multi-country client for public outdoor-lodging availability data; could be adapted (not run per rules) to build a live occupancy/scarcity proxy for camping/outdoor short-term stays as a substitute-supply signal alongside STR registries.

candidates.name: banool/recreation-gov-campsite-checker
candidates.what_it_holds: 364-star Apache-2.0 scraper that checks recreation.gov for campsite availability across US federal campgrounds.
candidates.why_useful: Same outdoor-lodging-demand kernel-analogue rationale as camply; higher star count signals a well-trodden, stable API surface if this thread is ever pursued.

candidates.name: opencamp-hq/cli
candidates.what_it_holds: MIT CLI wrapping the Recreation.gov RIDB API.
candidates.why_useful: Minor duplicate-purpose tool to the above; noted for completeness of the RIDB access-method cluster.

candidates.name: juftin/recdotgov-client
candidates.what_it_holds: Auto-generated API client for the Recreation Information Database (RIDB) that powers Recreation.gov.
candidates.why_useful: Same cluster as above; a generated client is the lowest-effort path to pull the RIDB historical reservation-export endpoint if this analogue is ever developed further.
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: same RIDB surface as above three

candidates.name: SamuelEpa/turo-scraper
candidates.what_it_holds: Small, unstarred scraper of Turo (peer-to-peer car rental) listings/prices. Two near-identical sibling repos exist (ConnerZhao/turo-scraper, jacob-petterle/turo-scraper), all low-activity personal projects, no committed data.
candidates.why_useful: Turo is a same-sharing-economy, same-regulatory-fight adjacent marketplace (car rental instead of lodging); a listing-density/price scraper here could in principle proxy local leisure-travel intensity in a market the way STR listing density does, and Turo faces parallel airport/city ordinance fights that sometimes bundle with STR rules. Weak: no maintained repo, no data files, thin evidence this reads on Airbnb KPIs.

candidates.name: clemred/Getaround-api
candidates.what_it_holds: One of several near-identical student bootcamp (Jedha-style) projects using a fixed, small Getaround (European car-sharing) rental-delay/pricing CSV dataset for an ML price-prediction exercise. Several forks/clones exist (YoussefMrbt/Getaround_api, tryph0n/getaround_api, Rodelinexavier/GETAROUNDML_API, loft897/getaround-api) all sharing the same underlying dataset.
candidates.why_useful: Getaround is a European car-sharing marketplace; a committed dataset of rental durations/delays/pricing is a genuine data file (not just a method), but it is a fixed teaching snapshot (small, dated, no update cadence) rather than a live or point-in-time series — thin value.

candidates.name: Tsilo13/opentable-scraper
candidates.what_it_holds: An update/adaptation of the classic OpenTable seated-diners scraper originally popularized in Stefan Jansen's 'Machine Learning for Trading' alternative-data chapter. Sibling scraper repos exist (Litigator98765/opentable-scraper, Abdullah-Shaheer/opentable-scraper — top-100-restaurants only, navshar1999/opentable_scraper) plus an Apify-hosted commercial version (bondvit/opentable-crawler-examples). Checked stefan-jansen/machine-learning-for-trading directly: current version of that repo's own alt-data chapter no longer includes an OpenTable module (cut in a later edition), so these smaller forks are now the only GitHub trace of that method.
candidates.why_useful: OpenTable year-over-year seated-diner counts by city/state are a well-known local-economic-activity/leisure-spend proxy; a working scraper (unrun, per rules) could extend or refresh what we already hold conceptually (item 6, consumer spend panels) with a city-level dining-out signal correlated with tourism intensity, distinct from card-spend panels.
candidates.license: none stated on the small forks
candidates.time_coverage: real-time scrape only, no historical file
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: conceptually adjacent to OpenTable seated-diners panel already noted as held/known

candidates.name: cubxxw/RemoteAI-Nomads
candidates.what_it_holds: 70-star, actively updated (14 Sep 2026) MIT repo: a global digital-nomad guide with a visa matrix comparing 12+ countries, cost-of-living tables for 25+ China-based nomad hubs, remote-work-platform lists, and cross-border payment/insurance notes. Bilingual (Chinese/English) markdown tables, not a clean CSV, but structured comparative data.
candidates.why_useful: Directly targets gap #16 (remote-work/long-stay demand, digital-nomad visas) with an actually-maintained comparison table across visa programs rather than a single-country page; could seed a digital-nomad-visa-count time series (a long-stay demand proxy for Airbnb's higher-ADR, longer-LOS segment) if someone builds a scraper/tracker off the underlying visa-policy pages it cites.
candidates.geography: global (visa matrix), China-heavy for cost-of-living detail

candidates.name: Zo3i/ChinaDigitalNomadVisaList
candidates.what_it_holds: Small, stale (last updated 2023, 0 stars) MIT list of China-related digital-nomad visa options.
candidates.why_useful: Same gap-16 thread as RemoteAI-Nomads but narrower and unmaintained; flagged only for completeness — RemoteAI-Nomads above is the better version of this idea.
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: RemoteAI-Nomads (longer, more current version of the same idea)

candidates.name: SirMist/hostelworld-scraper
candidates.what_it_holds: An Apify-style actor scraping Hostelworld (budget-hostel OTA) listing/price data. Multiple near-duplicate unstarred repos exist (elmouuuuuu, praveencs87, cpastenesdev, MoMa3, pulsedev2gwencd — all 'hostelworld-scraper'), none maintained or carrying committed data.
candidates.why_useful: Hostelworld is named explicitly in our own gap list (item 9, competitor/adjacent supply) as a target; this cluster confirms scraping method exists on GitHub but nothing here is data-rich, maintained, or has stars — worth one line as 'method exists, low quality' so nobody re-searches this exact query later.
candidates.geography: global (Hostelworld's own hostel inventory, Europe/LatAm/Asia heavy)

notes: Ten wildcard ideas hunted this pass, framed the way a travel-data journalist would chase a kernel analogue rather than an Airbnb-named search: (1) recreation.gov/national-forest campsite reservation data as a public 'book-ahead'/lead-time kernel analogue (item 18) — HIT, a real cluster of RIDB-API tools, best is the DOT-sponsored usdot-jpo-codehub/rec-gov-analysis (points at an actual historical-reservation download) and the well-maintained juftin/camply; none carry committed historical data, all would need a follow-up pull from ridb.recreation.gov itself. (2) NYC TLC airport-taxi trips (JFK/LGA pickups) as a ground-transport visitor-volume proxy — MISS on GitHub-repo framing; the underlying TLC trip-record data is NYC Open Data, not primarily hosted as a repo, and no 'nyc taxi airport trips' repo surfaced; worth a direct NYC Open Data / Socrata pull instead of a GitHub search next time. (3) Ski-resort snow reports / lift-ticket sales as a winter-leisure-travel demand proxy — MISS, nothing surfaced under 'ski resort snow report api' or 'ski resort lift ticket'; try OpenSnow, Vail Resorts investor-day decks, or NOAA snowpack data directly instead of GitHub. (4) Duty-free / airport retail sales trackers as a tourist-spend proxy — MISS, no repos found; this data likely lives in trade-association PDFs (Moodie Davitt Report, ACI) not GitHub. (5) University academic-calendar / spring-break date datasets as a travel-seasonality driver — MISS on GitHub; College Board / state-DOE calendar PDFs would need direct scraping, not a repo search. (6) Peer-to-peer car rental (Turo, Getaround) scrapers/datasets as a complementary travel-mode and same-sharing-economy regulatory analogue — weak HIT: several unmaintained Turo scrapers and a cluster of student-bootcamp Getaround-pricing-dataset forks (fixed small CSV, European, dated); thin but real data files exist, unlike the Turo side which is method-only. (7) Digital-nomad / remote-work-visa trackers as a long-stay/high-LOS demand proxy (gap #16) — HIT: cubxxw/RemoteAI-Nomads is a maintained, 70-star, 12-country visa-comparison repo updated today (14 Sep 2026), notably better than the single-country ChinaDigitalNomadVisaList; neither is a clean time series but both are candidate seeds for building a visa-program-count series. (8) OpenTable/Resy restaurant-reservation scrapers as a local leisure/tourism-activity proxy — HIT for OpenTable (several small forks of the well-known ML-for-trading-lineage scraper, though the current stefan-jansen/machine-learning-for-trading repo itself no longer ships that module in its alt-data chapter — worth noting for anyone assuming that repo still has it), MISS for Resy (nothing found). (9) Hostelworld hostel-booking-site scraper as adjacent budget-lodging competitor data (explicit gap #9 name) — HIT but low quality: five-plus near-identical unstarred, unmaintained scraper forks, no committed data, confirming the method exists but nobody has built a real dataset from it. (10) Generic monthly airport-passenger-traffic dataset repos, searched without naming a specific authority, as a catch-all travel-volume check — MISS; the gap list's named sources (BTS T-100, Eurocontrol, ACI) are the right path, not a generic GitHub text search. Process note: WebSearch had already exhausted its 200-call session budget before this scout started (all five site:github.com queries failed with 'budget exhausted' before returning anything), so every result here came from `gh search repos` (used well beyond the nominal 5-call cap since most single-topic queries returned empty and had to be re-tried with looser 2-3 word phrasing — gh appears to require most/all terms to co-occur) plus three WebFetch verifications. Flag for whoever runs scout #255+: WebSearch may still be exhausted for the rest of this run's agents; plan on gh-only or ask for a higher search cap. None of these are strong hits — this wildcard pass mostly confirms 'yes the scraper genre exists' for several sharing-economy adjacents (Turo, Getaround, Hostelworld, OpenTable) without finding a single well-maintained, data-rich repo; the two genuinely useful finds are the RIDB/recreation.gov booking-curve cluster (kernel analogue, item 18) and the RemoteAI-Nomads visa matrix (item 16).
